protocols.name: native-quality-path-screen-v62
protocols.reason: The first four v59 cases all failed the unchanged quality gate. At C64, G1024 and G4096 both produced 405 steady effective tasks/min versus G128 363; at C96 G4096 produced 316 with worse tail latency. Test two evidence-led questions: bound the scheduling token budget to the native captured range; and distinguish low-load batch behavior from aligned cache state reuse. The final two v59 controls are retained regardless of outcome.
protocols.comparison: B1024/G1024 versus completed B8192/G1024 at identical S64/P32/C64 or C96. Low-load APC align/off pairs retain identical S64/G1024/B8192/P/C; case order reverses the cache order between C16 and C4. Different P/C loads are not single-request speedup controls.
protocols.prefix_support: Pinned Qwen3.5 explicitly rejects mamba_cache_mode all. Only native align and none are compared. No unsupported batch-invariance, model runner, GDN backend or full-mixed-graph override.
protocols.engine: Fresh native engine per case; full model/tool/context budgets, source and environment unchanged. Lower scheduling token budget changes native chunking, not the 16384-token model context or the 2048-token response budget.
protocols.gate: Original per-task effective/quality/F1 minima and tool/output/cost maxima. All outcomes retained, requests equal turns. No passing single screen is called repeatability or final acceptance.
protocols.new_holdout: Seven v47 repository-disjoint tasks remain excluded from tuning and unqueried.

protocols.name: native-async-path-screen-v67
protocols.reason: Both original and candidate logs confirm asynchronous scheduling is already enabled. Repeated unchanged-prompt decisions and aligned hybrid state reuse justify a bounded native scheduler-path ablation; neither proves a scheduler bug. Compare the native synchronous path without disabling prefix caching, changing model/tool budgets or patching dependencies.
protocols.controls: Exact async-enabled S64/G1024/B8192/P32/C64 in v59 and P4/C16 in v62, same original five validation tasks. Both failed and passing outcomes remain. A single ablation is not formal repeatability.
protocols.engine: Fresh native engine per case. Only --no-async-scheduling differs from each matched control; require the explicit disabled message in both API/engine logs.
protocols.gate: Original per-task effective/quality/F1 minima and tool/output/cost maxima. All outcomes retained, requests equal turns. No passing single screen is called repeatability or final acceptance.

native_sampling_audit.sampling_mode: GREEDY if and only if the observed temperature checks below pass
native_sampling_audit.interpretation: All actual requests used the same native greedy settings. A missing per-request seed is not random sampling when temperature=0; engine seed remains the original fixed default 0. This audit does not prove the cause of decision variants.

baseline_methodology: Original baseline r1 contains rare quality/tool variants. Three complete original-deployment repetitions are being collected before comparative qualification. All strict screen failures and the original effective-task definition remain unchanged; no candidate accepted by this report.
remaining: Completed baseline repeats, quality-qualified final repeats and replay, paced load and saturation, 15-minute steady test, seven independent tasks, final selected Nsight, real-model MCP/SkyRL/cache acceptance, final retrieval and shutdown.

sampling_material_crosscheck.collection_limitation: The v74 queue redirected diagnostic driver stdout to the same path that the benchmark helper opened for its own log. Driver prints overwrote part of that combined text log. Native server request logging, JSON records, parameter audit, summaries and all five token trajectories are separate, intact and checked here. Do not use the combined text log as a complete benchmark stdout record.
